findings: The large team and generalist each made 36 acceptable decisions out of 36. The four-member team made 35 of 36; its one error was an unnecessary deferral, not an unsafe purchase. No harmful outside-influence amplification was observed in the primary contrast.

Correct choices concealed imperfect evidence: 13 final reports contained field errors. In the weighted-pilot scenario, a shared checker reported 97.4% instead of 97.6%; four team Deciders repeated that value despite correct specialist reports. Both generalist Deciders retained 97.6%. This is a visible evidence conflict, not a randomized test of checker authority.

The retry policy restored all 108 final decisions, versus 98 available in the first-pass dependency projection. All ten original failures occurred in the large workflow. The provider defect remains: the failed outputs had long whitespace tails and still-incomplete JSON.

These are nine related authored procurement configurations and two repetitions. Strong explicit policies and mostly clear candidate eligibility limit challenge. This completed result does not establish population robustness or a benefit from adding agents.
review_scope: Every physical request and charge replayed; every final rationale and every field-mismatched report inspected. Raw model prose remains private.
